report.executive_summary: Recomputation from the trusted table confirms A's headline result: all four WO-04 packages pass both policy gates, so lowest measured energy decides. Ranking: P1 6, P3 14, P2 40, P4 67 kWh per acceptance batch, with leader gaps +8, +34 and +61 kWh. A's gate arithmetic, ranking, ratios and P2-dominance claim all check out. One factual error found: A states a quality gate of 95 removes only P2; in fact P3 (89) also fails, so P2 and P3 are removed, leaving P1 and P4. The conclusion is unchanged — P1 still leads — but the stated check must be corrected before handover. Verdict: A's P1 recommendation is client-correct; the error is presentational, not decision-changing.
report.figure_caption: Verification chart: gate table for all four packages and measured energy bars 6/14/40/67 kWh with leader gaps +8/+34/+61; callout corrects A's gate-95 robustness claim.

recommendation.rationale: Independent recomputation confirms the client-correct winner: all four packages qualify, so lowest measured energy decides. P1's 6 kWh leads P3 by 8, P2 by 34 and P4 by 61 kWh, with near-best quality (98) and defects (1). The outcome survives the corrected robustness checks, and open questions cannot close the gaps. Correct A's gate-95 statement: it removes P2 and P3, not only P2.

sections.body: Quality gate (at least 80): P4 100, P1 98, P3 89, P2 86 — all pass; weakest margin is P2 at six points, matching A. Defect gate (at most 5): P1 1, P3 1, P2 5, P4 5 — all pass; P2 and P4 sit at the full allowance with zero margin, which still satisfies the rule. Every candidate qualifies, so the lowest-ID tie-break never activates: measured energies differ. This confirms A's gate section exactly, with no hidden weighting or severity adjustment permitted, since severity data is not supplied.
sections.heading: Gate recomputation: all four qualify

sections.body: Ascending energy gives P1 6, P3 14, P2 40, P4 67 kWh on the common batch/output/acceptance basis. Gaps to the leader: 14−6=8, 40−6=34, 67−6=61 kWh — all match A. Ratio checks: P3 uses 14/6=2.33x, P2 40/6=6.67x, P4 67/6=11.17x the leader's energy; A's rounded 2.3x/6.7x/11.2x are acceptable. Reduction shares: 8/14=57.1%, 34/40=85.0%, 61/67=91.0% — A's 57/85/91 percent confirmed. The only close comparison remains the 8 kWh P1–P3 margin; P2 and P4 deficits are far beyond plausible measurement noise.
sections.heading: Energy ranking and gap checks

sections.body: A's dominance claim is verified: P3 beats P2 on all three columns (89 vs 86, 1 vs 5, 14 vs 40 kWh), so P2 is strictly dominated. The P4 trade-off checks: two extra quality points (100 vs 98) cost 61 kWh and four extra defects. But A's robustness check is wrong: a quality gate of 95 does not remove only P2 — P3 at 89 also fails. P2 and P3 are removed; P1 (98) and P4 (100) survive, and P1 still leads at 6 kWh, so the decision stands while the stated check is factually incorrect. A's second check, a defect limit of 4 removing only P2 and P4, is correct (P1 and P3 sit at 1).
sections.heading: Dominance confirmed; one robustness error

sections.body: Measured facts are the trusted table's three columns on a stated common basis; A keeps these separate from unverified cost, delivery, maintenance and reliability fields, which are correctly excluded from ranking. Open items: single readings only, so repeat-run variance behind 6 and 14 kWh is unknown; defect severity data is absent. The delivered page-1 figure shows the energy bars in the correct 6/14/40/67 order at legible resolution; exact proportionality is verified numerically here rather than pixel-by-pixel. Given prior-round chart errors, C should re-check any restated figure against the table before handover.
